work: Eureka: A Prose Poem (New York: Putnam, 1848)
locator: Gutenberg ebook 32037 plain text, lines 2618-2634 (paragraph beginning 'No astronomical fallacy')
idea_year_note: publication year; from the Feb 1848 lecture
claim: If stars were endless the sky would glow uniformly; dark gaps could only mean light from the far background has not yet arrived. He grants this possible but sees no reason to believe it.
later_result: Finite light-travel time (with finite stellar lifetimes) resolves the dark-night-sky (Olbers) paradox
confirm_event: Kelvin, 'On Ether and Gravitational Matter through Infinite Space', Phil. Mag. ser. 6, 2:161-177 (Aug 1901), secs. 18-19 pp. 175-176
causal_source: Harrison, Darkness at Night (Harvard UP 1987) draws the parallel retrospectively; Kelvin 1901 cites neither Poe nor Olbers
same_passage_wrong: Concludes the Universe of Stars is bounded, with dark gaps as windows onto an empty 'Universe of Vacancy'; elsewhere says the cosmos is now collapsing
instrument: none: a calculation from star counts, light speed and solar-age estimates

locator: Gutenberg 32037 lines 725-745 (Particle irradiated spherically into vacant space); lines 3397-3402 (present state is 'progressive collapse')
claim: All matter began as one primordial Particle, irradiated outward into pre-existing empty space as finite atoms; gravity is their tendency to return, and the cosmos is now collapsing back to unity.
later_result: Expanding universe from a dense early state (Lemaitre 1927 theory; Hubble 1929 velocity-distance relation)
confirm_event: Hubble, 'A relation between distance and radial velocity among extra-galactic nebulae', PNAS 15(3):168-173 (1929)
causal_source: no citation of Poe in Lemaitre 1927/1931 or Hubble 1929
same_passage_wrong: Matter moves through pre-existing space (not expansion of space); asserts the present cosmos is in progressive collapse, the opposite of Hubble's recession; ends in a pulsating 'Heart Divine'
instrument: Mount Wilson 100-inch Hooker telescope with spectrograph (redshifts; Cepheid distances)

work: De luce seu de inchoatione formarum
locator: Baur (ed.), Die philosophischen Werke des Robert Grosseteste, BGPM 9 (1912), De luce pp. 51-59: point of light to sphere p. 51 ll. 10-12; nine celestial spheres p. 55 ll. 27-29; thirteen spheres p. 56
claim: God created a point of light that multiplied itself instantly in all directions, drawing matter into a sphere until rarefied, then forming nine celestial and four elemental spheres.
later_result: Big Bang: expansion from a dense early state
causal_source: Bower et al., Proc. R. Soc. A 470:20140025 (2014), arXiv 1403.0769, model it but claim no influence
same_passage_wrong: Instantaneous light; geocentric nested spheres; exactly nine heavens plus four elements; light as the form of corporeity
instrument: Mount Wilson 100-inch Hooker telescope with spectrograph

locator: KSA 9, notebook 11 (M III 1, spring-autumn 1881): 11[202] main statement; also 11[148], 11[152], 11[245], 11[269], 11[305]. Theorem: Acta Math. 13 ch. II sec. 8, Theoreme I p. 69
idea_year_note: notebook dated spring-autumn 1881; unpublished in his lifetime
claim: With a finite quantity of force and infinite time, every combination of states must already have occurred and must recur, infinitely often.
later_result: Poincare recurrence theorem: a bounded, volume-preserving dynamical system returns arbitrarily close to almost any initial state
confirm_event: Poincare, 'Sur le probleme des trois corps et les equations de la dynamique', Acta Mathematica 13:1-270 (1890)
same_passage_wrong: Exact identical recurrence of the whole world; the real universe is expanding and not a bounded phase space

work: Doctrine of ekpyrosis as reported by Diogenes Laertius
locator: Diogenes Laertius, Lives 7.134, 7.137 (periodic absorption and re-creation), 7.141-142 (Hicks tr. 1925)
idea_year_note: c. 300 BCE (Zeno); transmitted by Diogenes Laertius c. 3rd c. CE
claim: The cosmos is periodically consumed into fire and reconstituted from it, in an endless cycle governed by divine reason.
later_result: Ekpyrotic/cyclic cosmology: hot Big Bang produced by colliding branes, possibly repeated
confirm_event: Khoury, Ovrut, Steinhardt, Turok, Phys. Rev. D 64:123522 (2001) (a proposal, not a confirmation)
causal_source: KOST 2001 p. 3 and ref. 13 ('K. Volk and J. Katz, private communication'): name only
same_passage_wrong: Fire as the cosmic substance; providential divine reason; exact repetition; geocentric finite cosmos in a void

work: 'Die Ueberwindung des wissenschaftlichen Materialismus', lecture at the GDNA meeting, Luebeck
locator: Lecture of 20 Sept 1895, printed Leipzig: Veit 1895, pp. 25-27
claim: Matter and atoms are dispensable hypotheses; energy is the only reality science needs.
later_result: Molecular reality established by Brownian motion measurements
confirm_event: Perrin, Brownian-emulsion sedimentation counts, Comptes rendus 146:967 (May 1908)
causal_source: Ostwald, Vorbericht to Grundriss der allgemeinen Chemie, 4th ed. (1909; preface Nov 1908) cites Thomson's ion counts and Brownian motion; read in the 5th ed. (1917) reprint, goobi.tib.eu 1778037402
same_passage_wrong: Energetics: matter is only a spatial grouping of energies
instrument: high-power microscope with water-immersion objective counting emulsion grains

claim: Atoms are a provisional mathematical device, not real things; physics should not assert them.
later_result: Molecular reality established by Brownian motion measurements

locator: Mechanik 1883 Kap. II sec. 6 art. 5, pp. 216-217; McCormack tr. 1893 ch. II.vi.5 p. 232
claim: Newton's bucket shows only rotation relative to the earth and distant masses; with very massive walls the result might differ; inertia may be tied to distant matter.
later_result: General relativity's frame dragging (Lense-Thirring) by rotating mass
confirm_event: Everitt et al., Gravity Probe B final results, Phys. Rev. Lett. 106:221101 (2011)

same_passage_wrong: No law or mechanism offered; Mach rejected atoms in the same book and later disowned relativity
instrument: cryogenic gyroscopes in Earth orbit (Gravity Probe B)

work: 'Can quantum-mechanical description of physical reality be considered complete?', Phys. Rev. 47:777-780
locator: Phys. Rev. 47:777-780 (15 May 1935): reality criterion p. 777; no-real-change (locality) premise p. 779
claim: If a quantity can be predicted with certainty without disturbing a system it is an element of reality; with no action at a distance, quantum mechanics is therefore incomplete.
later_result: Bell-inequality violation: no local hidden-variable theory reproduces quantum predictions
confirm_event: Hensen et al., loophole-free Bell test, Nature 526:682-686 (2015)
causal_source: Bell, Physics 1:195 (1964) is titled on the EPR paradox; Hensen et al. 2015 abstract frames itself against it
same_passage_wrong: Concluded a local completion of quantum mechanics must exist
instrument: entangled electron spins in NV centres in diamond, 1.3 km apart, with fast random setting choice

locator: Discourse sec. 9; Leibniz's 4th paper to Clarke secs. 4-6
claim: No two substances can be exactly alike in all their properties; two indiscernible things would be one thing.
later_result: Quantum identical particles: permuting two same-kind particles gives no new state
confirm_event: Bose, 'Plancks Gesetz und Lichtquantenhypothese', Z. Phys. 26:178-181 (1924)

locator: Essai, 1st ed. (Paris: Courcier 1814) pp. 2-3, section 'De la probabilite'; 2nd ed. 1816 pp. 3-4
claim: An intellect knowing all forces and the positions of all bodies at one instant could compute the whole future and past with certainty.
later_result: Quantum uncertainty: position and momentum are not jointly sharp
confirm_event: Heisenberg, 'Ueber den anschaulichen Inhalt der quantentheoretischen Kinematik und Mechanik', Z. Phys. 43:172-198 (1927)
